answer: Seeded challenge divergence. Each new identity must solve a unique challenge kernel derived from its public key, then wander through a random challenge sequence whose answers depend on timing jitter observed at registration. Clones registered in one burst share correlated jitter and fail cross-checks against a quartz-stable clock reference, so the whole batch is discarded. The attacker pays full compute plus a nonrefundable registration deposit per attempt, while expected payout falls below zero once batch failure probability exceeds one half.
